tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Run a read-only... assessment... Use when asked to assess, audit, or review...'), focuses on user intent (assessing security of SageMaker workloads), lists extensive explicit trigger contexts (notebook exposure, KMS encryption, model isolation, endpoint HA, GuardDuty, MLOps governance, etc.), and clarifies scope boundaries (read-only, defers to another skill for access denial diagnosis). It is a dense but single-paragraph description appropriate for the complexity of the domain.
tests.evidence: "Run a read-only Amazon SageMaker AI security posture assessment across an AWS account, regions, and associated accounts. Use when asked to assess, audit, or review the security of Amazon SageMaker AI workloads: notebook and domain direct-internet exposure..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is domain-specific throughout — read-only constraints, verifiability contract, multi-region/account mechanics — without explaining generic concepts like what IAM or encryption is. It stays tight on project-specific conventions.
tests.evidence: Treat every account as production unless told otherwise.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/consistency-critical parts (read-only safety, verifiability contract, schema conformance) are highly prescriptive, while check execution itself defers detail to the reference file, appropriately matching rigor to risk.
tests.evidence: ONLY call `Describe*`, `List*`, `Get*`, `BatchGet*`, and equivalent read operations. NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes...

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present competing tool choices; it mandates a single read-only API approach without alternative tooling options to evaluate.
tests.evidence: No menu of competing tools/approaches is present in the body.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow is a generalizable procedure (confirm scope, resolve regions, run checks, assemble report, self-check) applicable to any assessment request, not a one-off declaration.
tests.evidence: Determine which **accounts** are in scope (default primary; or named IDs / "all accounts").

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit gotchas-style section covering the verify-vs-prescribe determinism contract, SM-02 mixed-check nuance, and read-denied handling — all non-obvious environment-specific corrections.
tests.evidence: **`SM-02` is a mixed check.** Its AmazonSageMakerFullAccess detection is **Heuristic**... Do not call `Generate*`, report those aspects as prescribe guidance in the resolution.
